text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm drafting the nodepool/scale policy for GPUs. Goal: clear rules for Dedicated vs Hosted pools (isolation, autoscale, cost/fallback). Want feedback before RFC Friday.

alex: Quick question — do we want node-level physical isolation for every enterprise tenant, or can some customers be namespace-isolated on shared GPU pools?

chris: For regulated customers we need node-level isolation + KMS + dedicated VPC. Namespace-only on shared pools is risky for high-sensitivity data.

maya: Agreed. My proposal: three classes: 
- private (VPC/on-prem) = full node/isolation + audit logs
- dedicated (reserved GPU node pools) = node-level isolation per-tenant, but can be shared across tenant-apps when same org
- hosted (multi-tenant) = shared GPU pools with strict namespace quotas and runtime privacy controls

sre-oncall: Autoscaler notes: CA can handle GPU node groups but we must ensure min/max per pool. For hosted pools set min=0 / scale-to-zero; for dedicated keep a small guaranteed min to meet SLAs (e.g., min 2 nodes).

alex: How do we avoid waste on dedicated? Reserved nodes are expensive when idle. Could we allow burst into hosted pools as fallback?

chris: Yes — routing policy that prefers dedicated but falls back to hosted (with explicit tenant consent). Must log fallbacks and obfuscate customer data in hosted fallback.

maya: Network/namespace plan: use NetworkPolicies + LimitRanges + ResourceQuotas on hosted. For dedicated: separate node pool + taints/tolerations + `redwood/tenant` node label.

infra-bot: Deployment note: created infra-ticket #1234 for policy config and CA changes — https://internal/infra/1234 :spiral_note_pad:

chris: Also consider preemptible/spot GPU nodes for hosted to cut costs. But preemptions require fast checkpointing and graceful fallback. Add retry/fallback logic in the serving layer.

maya: Eviction behavior — if a GPU pod is evicted on dedicated, we should: 1) attempt restart on same pool, 2) if insufficient capacity, failover to hosted pool per routing policy, 3) notify owner + SLO alert. Keep retries bounded.

alex: Cluster-autoscaler config suggestions:
```yaml
expander: least-waste
balance-similar-node-groups: true
scaleDownUtilizationThreshold: 0.2  # be conservative for GPU groups
nodeGroupMin: 0 (hosted)
nodeGroupMin: 2 (dedicated)
```

chris: Also add node taint pattern so pods land correctly:
```yaml
nodeSelector:\n  redwood/node-class: gpu
nodeAffinity:\n  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:\n    nodeSelectorTerms:\n      - matchExpressions:\n          - key: redwood/tenant\n            operator: In\n            values: ["customer-a"]\nTolerations:\n  - key: "redwood/tenant"\n    operator: "Equal"\n    value: "customer-a"\n    effect: "NoSchedule"\n```

maya: Runbook idea: if dedicated pool utilization < 30% for 7 days, infra creates consolidation ticket and contacts account owner with cost options.

sre-oncall: Monitoring — add per-pool dashboards (GPU utilization, pending pods, scale events, preemptions). Alert on P99 scheduling latency > 30s.

alex: One more: region constraints. Some customers require specific regions; we should allow pinned nodepools per-region and policy to avoid cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed.

maya: Next steps: I'll assemble RFC with these sections (isolation, autoscale config, taints/labels, fallback routing, runbook, dashboards). @alex @chris can you add concrete eviction numbers and quota defaults by EOD tomorrow? :thumbsup:
